fine_lines.title: melt vs dissolve
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان بمعنى «يذوب» لكن بطريقة مختلفة. melt: مادة صلبة تتحول إلى سائل بسبب الحرارة، مثل الثلج أو الآيس كريم أو الشوكولاتة. dissolve: مادة تختفي داخل سائل آخر وتختلط به، مثل السكر أو الملح في الماء؛ السكر لا يذوب بسبب الحرارة بل يختلط بالشاي.

examples.sentence: Eat your ice cream before it melts.
The butter melted in the hot pan.
Salt dissolves quickly in warm water.
Let the tablet dissolve in a glass of water.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean to become liquid, but in different ways. "Melt": a solid becomes liquid because of heat, like ice, ice cream or chocolate. "Dissolve": something disappears into a liquid and mixes with it, like sugar or salt in water. Sugar doesn't melt in tea because of heat; it mixes into the tea.

fine_lines.title: curb vs sidewalk
fine_lines.explanation_ar: sidewalk (وفي بريطانيا pavement) هو الرصيف نفسه الذي تمشي عليه بعيداً عن السيارات. أما curb (وفي بريطانيا kerb) فهو الحافة المرتفعة في طرف الرصيف التي تفصله عن الشارع الذي تسير فيه السيارات.

examples.sentence: The sidewalk was full of people.
Don't park too close to the curb.

fine_lines.explanation_en: The "sidewalk" (British: "pavement") is the path you walk on, away from the cars. The "curb" (British: "kerb") is the raised edge of the sidewalk that separates it from the road where cars drive.

fine_lines.title: stall vs vendor vs cart
fine_lines.explanation_ar: stall هو المكان الثابت الصغير (كشك أو طاولة) الذي يُباع منه. vendor هو الشخص البائع نفسه. cart هي عربة متحركة على عجلات يبيع منها البائع.

examples.sentence: She runs a flower stall in the market.
The ice cream vendor smiled at the kids.
He pushed his food cart down the street.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A "stall" is the small fixed place (a booth or table) where things are sold. A "vendor" is the person who sells. A "cart" is a small moving vehicle on wheels that the vendor sells from.

grammar.title: Talking about the future: present continuous vs going to vs will
grammar.explanation_ar: ثلاث صيغ للمستقبل بمعانٍ مختلفة. المضارع المستمر (am/is/are + ing) للترتيبات المؤكدة التي تم التخطيط لها واتُّخذت لها إجراءات (حجز، موعد). going to للنية الموجودة في الذهن بلا ترتيبات بعد. will صيغة مجردة: لقرار لحظي اتُّخذ الآن، أو لاحتمال حدوث شيء في المستقبل، أو لطلب وعد.
examples: I'm seeing the dentist next Tuesday. (arranged)
I'm going to learn French one day. (intention)
The phone is ringing. I'll answer it. (instant decision)
Will you marry me? (asking for a promise)
grammar.explanation_en: Three ways to talk about the future, with different meanings. The present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) is for fixed plans that are already arranged (a booking, an appointment). "Going to" is for an intention in your mind, with no arrangements yet. "Will" is the basic form: for a decision made right now, for something that may happen in the future, or for asking for a promise.

grammar.title: Going to for predictions based on evidence
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما ترى دليلاً أمامك يدل على أن شيئاً سيحدث، استخدم going to وليس will. مثل غيوم سوداء كثيفة تعني أن المطر قادم، أو طفل يلعب بمقص حاد قرب وجهه.
examples: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
Be careful! He's going to cut himself.
grammar.explanation_en: When you see evidence in front of you that something will happen, use "going to", not "will". For example, thick dark clouds mean rain is coming, or a child is playing with sharp scissors near their face.

grammar.title: Meanwhile
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم meanwhile لنقول إن شيئاً كان يحدث في نفس الوقت الذي حدث فيه شيء آخر. تأتي غالباً في بداية الجملة وبعدها فاصلة.
examples: Omar ordered a sandwich. Meanwhile, Ali tried everything.
I'll wash the dishes. Meanwhile, you can rest.
grammar.explanation_en: We use "meanwhile" to say that something was happening at the same time as something else. It usually comes at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma.

questions.explanation_en: Ice cream turns into liquid because of heat = melts.
